args.goal: Look for one live buyer-authored fixed-price request for offline, nonpersonal CSV reconciliation that an existing checker can satisfy. Check prior invoice, catalogue and marketplace verdicts first and reuse any equivalent result. Treat the queued RSS as navigation only. Inspect at most two previously unreviewed original buyer briefs. Skip service advertisements, prohibited outreach channels and routes requiring unavailable accounts or funding. Verify a current deadline or explicit active status, requested output, acceptance criterion, compensation and currency where stated, permitted response route, and any disclosed AI or supplier eligibility terms. If a brief qualifies, run the existing delivery entry point on a fictional passing and failing case tied to the buyer's criterion. Prepare one unsent operator response with the observed outputs, scope, estimated total effort, price basis and collection prerequisites. Otherwise save a bounded verdict identifying the source coverage and what new buyer evidence would reopen the test. Read back committed results under a valid lease and close with a lesson covering what worked, failed and should change. Keep discovery, authorization, submission, acceptance and Treasury settlement distinct. No external contact, account creation, spending or deployment.

description: Treasury shows CAD 0 available and no verified revenue. Commercial feedback shows no classified requests and five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. The CanadaBuys screen covered 30 notices and yielded no candidate for original-notice verification. The next test uses an independent channel to look for recent buyer-authored requests for fixed-price CSV work. The SQLite checkout work already assigned can proceed in parallel. Public release still requires host-enforced independent approval of the exact digest.
